basis: Spinal cord herniation and vertebral defects define myelomeningocele. Neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of denervation, not direct urinary tract disease.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder reflects denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct renal injury is not a defining or consistently common lesion.

basis: Defining brain abnormalities and cardiomyopathy (4/5); syndactyly 3/5 and scoliosis 2/5 support skeletal involvement. Strabismus/saccadic signs lack documented intrinsic ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and slow saccades each occur in 2/5, but establish ocular motor dysfunction without documented intrinsic eye damage; hyperemia is transient.

basis: Defining endocrine autoimmunity/oral candidiasis (68/68); ocular damage 30-79%, reduced acuity 4/5. Cap omits skin/hair/nails 36-49%, asplenia 40% and tympanosclerosis 32%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: chronic oral candidiasis is a cardinal manifestation (68/68); enamel hypoplasia also affects 67/93.
decisions.ocular: involved: keratoconjunctivitis, cataract and corneal stromal opacity occur in 30-79%; reduced visual acuity is reported in 4/5.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: nail dystrophy 35/72 and alopecia 38/106 qualify, but defining endocrine/immune/oral disease and more consequential ocular damage take priority.

basis: Isolated optic atrophy with visual loss in 2/2; explicitly classified as mitochondrial disease, reflecting an inherited mitochondrial metabolic defect.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorder, supported by its mitochondrial-disease ancestry, despite its isolated ocular presentation.

basis: SCID defined by absent functional T and B lymphocytes: immune deficiency and a blood-cell deficiency. Respiratory and intestinal infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: T-negative/B-negative SCID is defined by deficiency of two blood-cell lineages; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Acute conjunctival inflammation defines the site. Viral, bacterial and allergic causes account for most cases, supporting the mechanism axis across this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most acute conjunctivitis is infectious or allergic; these mechanisms apply to most patients across the umbrella, although irritant forms are exceptions.

basis: Chondrodysplasia and defining neuromuscular junction hyperexcitability/myotonia; ocular involvement includes visual impairment 80-99% and cataract 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: defining neuromuscular hyperexcitability involves the neuromuscular junction, included in this axis; skeletal dysplasia and muscle involvement also remain primary.

basis: Costovertebral dysostosis and pharyngeal atresia define the syndrome; tongue aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Ear shape and position do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: tongue aplasia/hypoplasia affects 30-79%; the defining pharyngeal atresia belongs to pulmonary, while mandibulofacial dysostosis is skeletal.

basis: Defining skeletal/dental defects; microcephaly/tremor 2/2, hypomyelination 1/2; cardiac hypertrophy/conduction defects 1/2. Cap omits fat loss and insulin resistance (1/2 each).

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS hypomyelination occurs in 1/2, with microcephaly and tremor in 2/2; neurologic disease accompanies the defining skeletal/dental phenotype.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining hepatosplenic disease (>80%); pulmonary infiltration/insufficiency affects >50%. Neurologic degeneration varies by subtype and is omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: splenic storage/infiltration with hepatosplenomegaly defines both major forms; spleen is explicitly included in the blood-organ axis.
decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic storage and hepatomegaly are defining manifestations across both neurovisceral and chronic visceral forms, rather than incidental complications.
